note:
v1, GIVE OR TAKE: THE OPENER, A SKELETON (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 03:20 GMT; the slot's word is TIME; Harry, 26 Nov: "a new clicky minimal techno climb - keep chirpers signature playing with time, space, instruments, mathy effects, polyrthythms etc and illusions"). 124 BPM, G minor, 136 bars, 4:23. Written by a generator; the form is arithmetic.

THE IDEA: TWO DECKS. Deck A is the grid and never moves: a bass drum on the four, one click on the off-beats, a bass, later a clap. Deck B is everything else (a sixteenth-note noise click, wooden tocks in a five against the sixteen, a dub chord), and a hand is on it: it is pushed ahead of the grid and dragged back behind it, as a DJ rides one record against another. Nothing on deck B is placed by hand. One function of time, d(t), says how far its record is ahead; every event sounds when the record reaches it; and where the deck runs fast, what has a pitch on it goes sharp, as a record does. So the tempo you hear moving is real on one deck and false on the other, and the bass drum says which.

LISTEN FOR: 0:31, the sixteenth clicks starting to lean ahead of the off-beat click and fall back, once every two bars (24 ms at the furthest; 39 ms from 1:02, where the chord comes in and is never quite in tune). 1:33: THE BASS DRUM STOPS. For twelve bars deck B is alone and its tempo swings between 100 and 148; the chord sinks nearly four semitones and rises three. Does it sound like the track itself slowing and speeding? At 1:56 the bass drum comes back exactly where it always was, deck B is still swinging round it, and by 2:04 it is pulled in. 2:50: deck B is taken a whole sixteenth ahead and let back, four times; at the far point everything fits again, one step out. 3:21: the hand comes off.

MEASURED, not heard: the chord's lowest note in the render follows the speed (asked -2.08 semitones, read -2.06; asked +2.79, read +2.88). In the fullest section each part's strokes against the mix: bass drum +1.4 dB, bass 0.0, chord -3.3, grid click -7.3, tocks -8.6, clap -10.5; the sixteenth click averages 16.5 dB under the mix (in my first mix the grid click's strokes stood 23 dB under and the sixteenth click 31: inaudible; the clicks came up 14 to 17 dB and the chord and bass down). Beside the album's envelope (Aphex Twin's techno, I Feel Love: not click records): 8 to 10 dB short at 70-135 Hz, 9 over at 2.2 kHz (the tocks) and at 10-13 kHz (the sixteenth click): a click record against records that are not. 95.37 / 95.48 (seeds 0 and 11); rhythm reads 67: the scorer hears almost nothing off the grid (4%), so deck B is still quiet against deck A.

WHAT IT IS NOT YET: a skeleton. Six sounds; no fills, no transitions but the stops; the bass is a sine with a second harmonic; nothing happens in the last minute but parts leaving.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

v5, THE LOOP, AND ZENO'S BAR (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 07:51 GMT; round 5; not on v4's list: it is the one thing a hand does to a record that the song had not done). `C11T1_ROLL=0` writes v4 byte for byte.

WHAT IS NEW: the last four bars of "the nudge" (3:13 to 3:21) deck B is put in a LOOP, and the loop is cut in half, and in half again: the oldest way a DJ has of getting to the drop. A bar of the record's first beat, four times over; a bar of its first half beat, eight times; a bar of its first quarter, sixteen (every sixteenth is now the record's first instant: its drum, its click and its tock). Nothing is placed by hand: the record's position is still one function of time, now a sawtooth, and deck A plays straight on under it. THE LAST BAR IS ZENO'S: every loop gets sixteen turns and is half as long as the one before, so the sixteen take two beats, then one, then a half, a quarter ... and the bar line is reached only in the limit. The loop now holds one thing, the first instant of deck B's drum, and in the bar's last beat it stops being a rhythm: sixty-six strokes a second is a NOTE. It is the tempo's own note (124 to the minute, five octaves up: a C, 19 cents sharp; the song is in G minor), and it goes up an octave every time the loop is halved, to 2116 Hz, faster and faster, with deck A's bass drum taken out from under it. The loop is let go on the first beat of "locked", where the meeting tune's three notes are.
LISTEN FOR: 3:13 the record sticks on its first beat. 3:15 twice as fast; 3:17 sixteenths. 3:19 Zeno's bar: a roll (two beats), a flutter (one), and then in the last beat a note that climbs out of it, five octaves in half a second. 3:21 the drop.

In Zeno's bar the loop alone is within 4.2 dB of the whole mix in every loop (-1.5 -1.2 +0.3 -1.8 -4.2 -2.5 +0.8 +2.1 dB): it is the bar. Deck B's drum strikes 4, 8 and 16 times in the three bars before, and stands 10.8, 8.2 and 5.1 dB under the mix. Under 70 Hz Zeno's bar has 8.4 dB less than the bar before it, and "locked" has it back. The last loop ends 7.6 ms before the bar line; deck B's first drum of "locked" is on it. 97.35 / 97.36 (seeds 0 and 11); v4 re-read today 97.24: +0.11, a new best.
COSTS, disclosed: the fourth nudge is gone (the hand is off by the bar the loop starts: the reach in bars 100 to 104 was 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 0.25 sixteenths and is 0.25, 0, 0, 0, 0). The dub chord is silent for those four bars (it is not in the record's first beat); its echo rings over them. The scorer's recurrence share is 0.268 against a floor of 0.25 (v4: 0.272): ON THE EDGE, as it was. Every section cut is clear of the threshold (the nearest reads 0.177 against 0.15).

note:
v6, ZENO'S RECORD (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 09:06 GMT; round 6; a new row of eight bars: the song is 144 bars, 4:39). `C11T1_STRETCH=0` takes it out and writes v5 byte for byte.

WHAT IS NEW: the song has slowed deck B three ways: the hand (its pitch sags), the stop (its pitch falls five octaves), the loop. Now a fourth, which a hand cannot do: THE STRETCH. In a new row, "the stretch" (2:50 to 3:06, after "both"), deck B's record goes at half speed and ITS PITCH DOES NOT MOVE. It is done the way a machine does it: the record is cut into grains a sixteenth long, and each grain is played whole, at full speed, but the next grain starts only half a sixteenth further into the record. So everything on the record is played twice: every stroke becomes two, half a sixteenth apart, and the second is where the stroke would be on a record at half speed. Two bars on, a quarter of its speed: four strokes for each, three quarters of a sixteenth apart, a ratchet that runs up to the place and lands on it. Then an eighth: eight strokes, seven eighths apart. Then a sixteenth: sixteen strokes, fifteen sixteenths apart, which is very nearly deck A's grid: a click that starts a sixteenth late and is 8 ms less late every stroke until it is ON the grid, and the dub chord with it, a sliver that grows into a chord.
The record gets through a bar, then half a bar, a quarter, an eighth: a bar and seven eighths in eight bars, and going on like this it would never reach the end of its second bar. That is Zeno's other paradox (the runner). Its limit is the loop that follows in "the nudge": a record stretched for ever is one grain, repeated. So the song now has both: the loop halved until it is a note, and the speed halved until the record stands still.
Deck A's drum, bass and clap stand back for these eight bars (the song's one breakdown); its click stays, the ruler the stretched record is read against.
LISTEN FOR: 2:50 the drum and bass go; deck B at half speed, every stroke a flam. 2:54 ratchets of four into each beat. 2:58 rolls of eight. 3:02 the click sliding onto the grid, twice, and the chord growing. 3:06 everything back, and the hand's nudges.

MEASURED, not heard: the hat alone, 127 strokes read (not the one on the window's first sample), every one within 1.00 ms of where it is written; the gap inside a run 61.2, 90.7, 105.6, 113.2 ms (written 60.5, 90.7, 105.8, 113.4). In the master's hat band all 128 are found within 1.25 ms. At a sixteenth of its speed the hat is 114, 106, 99 ... 15, 8, 0 ms late on deck A's grid, twice. The knock alone: 24 strokes within 1.25 ms. THE PITCH: the tock in the stretch reads within 6 cents of the same notes where the decks are locked; in "both", under the hand, it reads -152 to +138 cents. 96.42 / 96.35 (seeds 0 and 11).
THE BASELINE: v5 re-read under the ensemble is 95.75 / 95.83 (the board's 97.35 was the single cut), so v6 is +0.67 / +0.52 on the same scorer and goes in with --keep.
TRIED AND REFUSED: the stretch with all of deck A under it (STRETCH_OVER=kick,tick,sub,clap): 95.78 / 94.28. The scorer did not find the row at all, and the song's only return was its last five seconds, standing on one cut (novelty 0.171 and 0.162 against a cut at 0.17). With the breakdown the row is a section (cuts 0.41 and 0.33), what follows it returns to what came before it (returns 4 of 7, share 0.50, no longer on the floor), and the stretch can be heard.
COSTS, disclosed: the row is 10 dB quieter than its neighbours (-20 against -10.5 dB) and the rest of the song is about 0.2 dB louder for it; spectrum 93.1 -> 88.7 and cohesion 94.0 -> 89.4 (eight bars with no bass). A stroke that began before a grain is not heard inside it (a real stretch would play its tail): only starts are stretched. The hat's small accents fall on other strokes after the new row (they count bars); nothing else after it differs. Both seams are as they were (the last four bars read -27.98 against -28.05).
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

A record's pitch is its speed: four to three is a perfect fourth, so everything on deck B is a fourth up: its G minor is C minor, over deck A's G. A CORRECTION FIRST, to my own earlier notes: A SEND IS TAKEN AFTER THE TRACK'S GAIN AND AFTER ITS PAN. I wrote the opposite in Out of Step v7's note, in its recipe row and to chirp-eco ("a send is pre-gain"), and in this song's v8 plan ("the echo is the larger part of the chord"). Benched today on one chord through this song's dub bus: 20 dB less track gain is 20 dB less echo; 20 dB less send is 20 dB less echo; the same chord panned hard to one side sends 4.7 dB less. WHAT IS NEW: every way deck B has left the grid so far has been a HAND or a SWITCH: a push, a drag, a stop, a spin, a speed. This one is an accident, and it is the one everybody who has owned a record knows. One turn of a platter at 33 is 1.81 seconds, and at this tempo that is FIFTEEN sixteenths: a turn of the groove holds a bar less its last sixteenth. In the second row of "both" (bars 73 to 80, 2:19.3 to 2:34.8) the needle does not cross into the next turn: it jumps back and plays the same turn again, with a pop, eight times. Deck A does not know. So against the grid the record's bar is a sixteenth short and arrives a sixteenth EARLIER every time round: 15 against 16, by accident.
WHAT THAT DOES, with no note changed:
- the wooden tock's five strokes (0 3 6 9 12 of sixteen) lose their long last gap and become dead even, every three sixteenths, for seven and a half bars: three against the beat's four;
- deck B's drum goes round deck A's, a sixteenth earlier a turn: with it, just before it, half way between (the two drums are then eighths), just after it, with it again, and round once more;
- the dub chord creeps back from the sixth sixteenth of the bar, a sixteenth a turn;
- half a bar before the row ends a hand puts the needle on (the eighth pop) and the record is where the grid is.
THE TURN IS IN THE RECORD'S BEATS, not the grid's: the platter is still being pushed and dragged (the hand of "both" is on it), so each time round takes as long as the platter takes (1742 to 1883 ms) and the tock and chord are as sharp or flat as they were going to be. Only what the needle reads has changed.
LISTEN FOR: 2:19 the row begins as before. 2:23 a dull pop, and the same bar starts again a sixteenth early; the tock straightens out. By 2:27 deck B's drum is between deck A's. 2:34 the last pop, and half a bar later everything is back.

The tock's gaps are 3 sixteenths of the grid (2.8 to 3.3: the hand) until the needle is put on, and 4 once after. The drum's are 4 (3.7 to 4.3) and, at each jump, 3. The pops are 14.4 to 15.6 sixteenths apart (mean 14.95).
The pop alone is 6 dB under deck A's click over 30 ms (-31.7 for -25.8 dBFS) and over a tenth of its peak for 6 ms. At my first fader (-14 dB) it was 27 dB under: benched and raised before any full render.
IN THE MASTER (seed 0, against v9, one speaker): the first turn (most of bar 73) is v9 to 78 dB: it is the record playing. The row is as loud as it was (-10.49 dBFS both) and no bar of it moves more than 0.23 dB. EVERY OTHER BAR IS v9: no gain change (0.001 dB), 78 dB under the music before the row and 65 dB after it, 73 dB in the last four bars (the seam into Least Common).

WHAT IS NEW: a scratch. Until now the hand has pushed the platter and dragged it. Now it takes hold of the record and RUBS it. Under the needle is deck B's dub chord. The hand goes round like a crank, and the record goes forward over the chord's start and back again: there and back in a beat (twice), in half a beat (twice), in a quarter of a beat (four times). Time goes forward and backward under the needle.
NOTHING IS A SAMPLE. A record's sound is its speed: its pitch is the speed, and so is its loudness (a pickup gives the groove's speed, not its place). So the chord is simply HELD for the bar, and three lanes are the physics. The pitch is the hand's speed. The loudness is the speed times what the record holds at the place under the needle: the chord, loud at its start and dying. The brightness is what the record holds there too: the chord's filter, open at its start and closing.
SO EACH RUB IS TWO SOUNDS. Forward: the chord's start goes under the needle exactly on the sixteenth, at exactly the record's own speed (the chord at its own pitch); the hand quickens and the chord bends up a tritone (the crank's fastest is root two times the record's speed: Eb3 G3 Bb3 D4 becomes A3 C#4 E4 G#4); it slows to a stop inside the chord: silence. Backward: the same piece of record the other way: quiet and dull first, swelling and brightening up to the chord's START, where it is cut off dead: a sound that ends with its own attack. Then the hand turns round in the silence before the chord and brings the start under the needle again on the next beat. A rub sounds for three quarters of its time.
